title: SRM Medical College Hospital Inaugurates National Conference on Regenerative Biology and Bioengineering, TRBB 2026
summary: SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre in Chennai has inaugurated TRBB 2026, a three-day national conference on translational regenerative biology and bioengineering.
body_html:
Chennai, 4 November 2026: SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre (SRMMCHRC), through its Division of Medical Research, has inaugurated the National Conference on Translational Regenerative Biology and Bioengineering (TRBB 2026). The three-day conference is being held from 3 to 5 November 2026 and brings together researchers, clinicians, academicians, industry professionals and students to examine new developments in regenerative medicine, biomedical engineering and translational healthcare research.

The conference offers a multidisciplinary platform for scientific exchange and collaborative research, with sessions focusing on tissue regeneration, stem cell biology, biomaterials, organoids, lab-on-a-chip technologies and theranostics. The inaugural programme was attended by academicians, researchers and scientific experts from leading institutions across the country.

Speaking on the importance of interdisciplinary biomedical research, Dr. R. Jayanthi, Dean (Medical), SRMMCHRC, said, “The future of healthcare lies in collaborative research, bringing together clinicians, biologists, engineers, and researchers to transform scientific discoveries into meaningful improvements in human health.”

Dr. Sunil K. Narayan, Dean Research (MHS) and Convener, TRBB 2026, said, “The ultimate goal of scientific research is to translate discoveries into better treatments for people suffering from diseases and injuries. Bridging the gap between basic science and clinical practice is essential to advancing healthcare and improving human lives.”

Prof. Sarit Kumar Das, V. Balakrishnan Chair, IIT Madras, described the human body as nature’s finest engineering marvel, stating, “Whatever an engineer tries to design is already present in the human body, in a much better way.” Dr. Joy Varghese, Director and HOD, Hepatology and Transplant Hepatology, Gleneagles Hospital, Chennai, said, “The future of healthcare lies in turning scientific discoveries into life-changing treatments. Regenerative biology and bioengineering offer exciting possibilities to transform medicine. Let us bring science and clinical practice together to create innovations that truly make a difference to human lives.”

The programme includes keynote lectures, invited talks, workshops, poster presentations and flash talks, with speakers from the Indian Institutes of Technology, CSIR laboratories and other research organisations. The keynote speakers include Prof. Suman Chakraborty of IIT Kharagpur and Prof. Sarit Kumar Das of IIT Madras. Dr. Snehasis Mishra, Assistant Professor, Division of Medical Research, SRMMCHRC, and Dr. M. Parani, Professor and Chairperson, School of BioEngineering, SRMIST, were also present at the inauguration.

The organisers said TRBB 2026 places particular emphasis on young researchers and students, giving them the chance to interact with established scientists and gain exposure to advanced research methods. Through the conference, the Division of Medical Research at SRMIST aims to strengthen the biomedical research ecosystem and bridge the gap between fundamental scientific discoveries and their practical use in healthcare.
